Native-safe replacement for the shared web <Select> (no DOM <select> on native): the inline SelectField — a Pressable trigger (current option label + '\u25BE' caret) that opens a transparent fade <Modal> popover whose options are accessible Pressable rows (accessibilityRole menu/menuitem, accessibilityState.selected), backed by a tap-to-close backdrop + onRequestClose. Same popover idiom as the already-ported IntervalSelect/Combobox/DataTableColumnsMenu; keeps both call sites (vehicle filter + auto-refresh) on one reusable control, and `find(o => o.value === value)` makes the empty-value 'All Vehicles' / '0' Default trigger labels resolve correctly.

Verified NO DOM-only modules, browser HTML elements (div/h3/p/button/input/select), lucide-react, Recharts, Leaflet, clsx, react-i18next, or old web ui components are imported — only react-native primitives (Modal/Pressable/ScrollView/TextInput/View) plus the existing shared native AppText, theme tokens (colors/shadows/spacing), and the sibling ported Toggle. State names (settings/name/icon), the reset-effect dependency array, handleSave logic, vehicleOptions/refreshOptions transforms, every i18n key + English fallback (incl. the dynamic dashSettings.refresh${value} keys), and the {value,label} option contract are preserved verbatim. A focused parity test (__tests__/DashboardSettingsModalParity.test.tsx) renders the open dialog (all four sections + name + default select labels), asserts Save-with-no-edits commits settings + closes without rename/icon, asserts rename trims + reports via onRename, asserts emoji pick reports via onChangeIcon, and exercises the SelectField popover to commit a vehicleId via onUpdate. Gates run from apps/native: npm run typecheck; npm run lint -- --quiet; npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles.
